# Implementation differences

Each case is a behaviour in which the implementations of the KS10 differ.
The levels A, B and open and the rules for them are in
[`conformance.md`](conformance.md). The sources of each case are in
[`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), [`unknowns.md`](unknowns.md) or
[`emulator.md`](emulator.md).

Columns: the choice of `ks10-core-uop` (uop), `ks10-core-soft` (soft) and
the pipelined core, and the comparison in each differential run. A
comparison is exact, mask (the differing fields are not compared), skip
(the case is not compared) or not-generated (the run makes no such case).
The programs are not assembled or run yet.

## Predicates

The operands of a case (`when` in the table):

- `any`: every case of the instructions.
- `left_shift_over`: a left shift by more places than the value for the instruction.
- `count_minus_256`: E with bit 18 set and bits 28 to 35 clear: a count of -256.
- `imul_negative_product_over_word`: a negative product of magnitude 2^35 + 1 to 2^36 - 1.
- `idiv_min_by_unit`: a dividend of -2^35 and a divisor of 1 or -1.
- `div_min70_by_zero`: a dividend of -2^70 and a divisor of 0.
- `hlle_positive_bits_1_3`: a positive source word with a bit of 1 to 3 set.
- `div_high_equals_divisor`: the high word of the magnitude of the dividend equals the magnitude of the divisor.
- `start_flags`: an instruction of the case that starts with one of the flags set.
- `lost_bit_before_last_step`: a left shift that loses a bit in a step before the last step, and none in the last step.
- `exponent_difference_over`: an exponent difference of more than n.
- `unnormalized_operand`: an operand that is not normalized.
- `page_fail`: a reference that page-fails.

## Cases

### aprid

The APRID word.

- Instructions: APRID; operands: `any`.
- Differs: mem.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "APRID of the ITS microcode".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (inout.50, APRID; its.15 UCV, HWOPT, HWSER; ks10.47 OPT): 020406,,003301.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, pdp10-ks, set cpu its): DSKCA prints CPU#=4097, MCV=416, MCO=570.

Program:

```
	APRID 100		; C(100) <- the processor ID
	HALT .
```

### pi-request-off-level

A program interrupt request on a level that is off.

- Instructions: WRPI; operands: `any`.
- Differs: pc.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Program interrupt requests on levels that are off".

Sources:

- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, 4.1, WRPI bits 24 and 26): the request counts also on a level that is off.
- microcode **[microcode]** (inout.50, LOADPI): a program request counts only on a level that is on.

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[JSR INT]
	MOVEM 1,42		; the instruction of level 1 (EPT at 0)
	MOVEI 2,1
	WRPI 4300		; PI on, a request on level 1; level 1 stays off
	JFCL
	HALT .			; AC 2 = 1: no interrupt
INT:	0
	MOVEI 2,2		; AC 2 = 2: the interrupt came
	HALT .
```

### rdubr-bits-0-2

Bits 0 and 2 of the RDUBR word before a WRUBR sets them.

- Instructions: RDUBR; operands: `any`.
- Differs: mem.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Bits 0 and 2 of the RDUBR word".

Sources:

- KSDEFS **[its]** (ksdefs.194, RDUBR): always returns 4.9 and 4.7 set.
- microcode **[microcode]** (inout.50, WRUBR, RDUBR): UBR AND 507703,,777777: the bits are 0 until a WRUBR sets them.

ITS sets both bits with each WRUBR, so the sources agree for ITS.

Program:

```
	RDUBR 100		; after a reset, before any WRUBR
	HALT .
```

### movsrj-ac

EXTEND MOVSRJ: the AC at the end.

- Instructions: EXTEND; operands: `any`.
- Differs: ac.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "The AC of MOVSRJ at the end".

Sources:

- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, 2.12, MOVSRJ): AC bits 9-35 hold the number of source bytes skipped.
- microcode **[microcode]** (extend.4, MVSKP, MOVST3): AC bits 9-35 are 0.

Program:

```
	MOVEI 1,5		; source: 5 bytes
	MOVE 2,[440700,,SRC]
	MOVEI 4,3		; destination: 3 bytes
	MOVE 5,[440700,,DST]
	EXTEND 1,[017000,,0	; MOVSRJ
		  0]		; fill
	HALT .			; AC 1: 2 skipped bytes, or 0
SRC:	ASCII /ABCDE/
DST:	0
```

### fad-large-exponent-difference

FAD with an exponent difference of 54 or more.

- Instructions: FAD; operands: `exponent_difference_over` (n 60).
- Differs: ac.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "FAD with a large exponent difference".

Sources:

- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, 2.3, footnote to FAD): 0 for the smaller operand above 72; from 54 to 72 a negative operand becomes all ones.
- microcode **[microcode]** (flt.5, FAD to FAS4): the full shift; a negative operand always becomes all ones.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, FAD): 0 for a difference of 65 or more.

The differential run makes exponent differences of 60 or less for all floating point instructions (oracle.rs, near).

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[201400,,0]	; 1.0
	FAD 1,[700400,,0]	; -2^-66: an exponent difference of 66
	HALT .
```

### ash-left-many

ASH and ASHC: a left shift of many places.

- Instructions: ASH, ASHC; operands: `left_shift_over` (ASH 28, ASHC 29).
- Differs: ac, flags:AROV,TRAP1.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "ASH and ASHC: a left shift of many places".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, ASHL, ASHC): one place for each step, up to 255 places.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, ASH, ASHC): a shift of a 64-bit integer; 140 places give the shift by 12.

Program:

```
	MOVE 13,[717711,,575334]
	ASH 13,214		; 140 places
	JSP 2,.+1		; the flags in AC 2
	HALT .
```

### shift-count-minus-256

A shift count of -256.

- Instructions: ASH, ASHC, LSH, LSHC; operands: `count_minus_256`.
- Differs: ac.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Shift count -256".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (ks10.47, SCADB SHIFT): bits 18 and 28-35 of E: -256 places.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, ASH, LSH, ASHC, LSHC): 0 places; ROT and ROTC use 256.

Program:

```
	MOVEI 1,1
	ASH 1,400000		; bit 18 set, bits 28-35 clear
	JSP 2,.+1
	HALT .
```

### circ

CIRC.

- Instructions: CIRC; operands: `any`.
- Differs: ac.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "CIRC".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (its.15 CIRC=1; simple.42, CIRC): the instruction exists (opcode 247).
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, case 0247): not compiled for the KS10: nothing changes.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2a, KLH10_I_CIRC): the instruction exists; 318 cases agree with ks10-core-soft.

The ITS microcode has CIRC; the PRM does not define it.

Program:

```
	MOVEI 3,1
	SETZ 4,
	CIRC 3,3
	HALT .
```

### fdv-quotient

FDV with normalized operands: bit 35 of the quotient.

- Instructions: FDV, FDVL, FDVM, FDVB, FDVR, FDVRI, FDVRM, FDVRB; operands: `any`.
- Differs: ac, mem.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "FDV: the quotient".

Sources:

- DSKCB **[manual]** (DSKCB.SEQ page 32, test P7700): an unnormalized divisor: 777375,,773771.
- uop **[measured]** (2026-11-28, ks10-core-uop, tests/instructions.rs, fdv_quotients_of_the_microcode): the quotient of ks10-core-soft and KLH10 in four cases.
- SIMH **[measured]** (2026-11-27, sims 9556eca0, oracle.rs without skip): 744 of 2075 cases differ in bit 35; FDVRB with a dividend of 0 leaves E unchanged.
- KLH10 **[measured]** (2026-11-27, KLH10 6d733f2a): agrees with ks10-core-soft in 2123 cases.

Level A, open until a source decides it (docs/conformance.md). The SIMH skip covers all FDV cases, not only those that differ.

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[152653,,256164]
	FDV 1,[631006,,651626]	; 573116,,702671 or 573116,,702672
	HALT .
```

### imul-negative-overflow

IMUL: a negative product that does not fit.

- Instructions: IMUL, IMULI, IMULM, IMULB; operands: `imul_negative_product_over_word`.
- Differs: flags:AROV,TRAP1.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "IMUL: a negative product that does not fit".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, IMUL to IMUL3): Overflow if the high word is not 0 or all sign bits.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, IMUL): no Overflow for a magnitude from 2^35 + 1 to 2^36 - 1.

Program:

```
	MOVEI 5,17
	MOVE 2,[750330,,434634]
	IMULB 5,2
	JSP 3,.+1
	HALT .
```

### idiv-min-by-unit

IDIV of -2^35 by 1 or -1.

- Instructions: IDIV, IDIVI, IDIVM, IDIVB; operands: `idiv_min_by_unit`.
- Differs: ac, flags:AROV,TRAP1,NODIV.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "IDIV of -2^35 by 1 or -1".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, IDIV, DIV1): only a divisor of 0 is tested.
- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, page 2-14): on the KS10, -2^35 by -1 gives -2^35 without an error.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, IDIV): No Divide.

Program:

```
	MOVSI 1,400000
	IDIV 1,[-1]
	JSP 3,.+1
	HALT .
```

### div-min-by-zero

DIV of -2^70 by 0.

- Instructions: DIV, DIVI, DIVM, DIVB; operands: `div_min70_by_zero`.
- Differs: ac, mem, flags:AROV,TRAP1,NODIV.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "DIV of -2^70 by 0".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, DIV1): No Divide; nothing is stored.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, DIV): no flag; DIVB stores 400000,,1.

Program:

```
	MOVSI 14,400000
	SETZ 15,
	DIVB 14,ZERO
	JSP 3,.+1
	HALT .
ZERO:	0
```

### hlle-klh10

HLLE of a positive word with a bit of 1 to 3 set.

- Instructions: HLLE, HLLEM, HLLES; operands: `hlle_positive_bits_1_3`.
- Differs: ac, mem.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "HLLE in KLH10".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, HLLE): the left half does not change.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2a, inhalf.c, kn10ops.h op10m_trz): bits 1 to 3 are cleared.

Program:

```
	HLLE 1,[100000,,123456]	; 100000,,0 or 0
	HALT .
```

### div-high-equals-divisor

DIV: the high word of the dividend equals the divisor in magnitude.

- Instructions: DIV, DIVI, DIVM, DIVB; operands: `div_high_equals_divisor`.
- Differs: ac, mem, flags:AROV,TRAP1,NODIV.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "DIV in KLH10: a high word equal to the divisor".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, DIVB, DIVC, NODIV): No Divide.
- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, page 2-14, DIV): No Divide if the high word is greater than or equal to the divisor.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2a, kn10ops.c, ddivstep): 400000,,0 without an error for a negative quotient.

The KLH10 skip does not test the sign of the quotient.

Program:

```
	MOVE 7,[777777,,777750]
	SETZ 10,
	DIV 7,[30]
	JSP 3,.+1
	HALT .
```

### trap-flags-clear

Trap 1 and Trap 2: a later flag word clears them.

- Instructions: ADD, SUB, MOVN, MOVM, AOJ, AOS, SOJ, SOS, DADD, DSUB, DMOVN, DMOVNM, DMUL, JFCL, PUSHJ, JSR, JSP; operands: `start_flags` (flags ['TRAP1', 'TRAP2']).
- Differs: flags:TRAP1,TRAP2.
- Level B: The case shows only with traps off: with traps on, the trap instruction clears the trap flags (PRM 1982, p. 2-78). With paging off, the PRM says that the trap flags have no effect, and it does not say that a later instruction clears them (p. 2-78). No DEC KS10 diagnostic tests the case: DSKDA clears TRAP 1 and TRAP 2 in its simulated flags (DSKDAM, SENTRY, CHECK; a reading of the KLAD sources, 2026-11-27).
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Trap 1 and Trap 2: each flag word loads them".

Sources:

- DPE9 **[microcode]** (M8620-0-DPE9 rev B, E60, E85, E78; ks10.47, MACROS -- PC FLAGS): each word with SPEC/FLAGS loads Trap 1 and Trap 2, so it clears a trap flag that it does not set.
- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, p. 2-78, overflow trapping): an overflow sets Trap 1; the trap instruction clears the trap flags; nothing else clears them.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c): as the PRM.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, kn10ops.c): as the PRM.
- KS10FPGA **[emulator]** (KS10FPGA 5090e7a1, pcflags.v): as the microcode.

Run with paging off, so that traps are off (ksdefs, WREBR 2.5). The instructions are those with a word of SPEC/FLAGS (discrepancies.md).

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[377777,,777777]
	ADD 1,[1]		; overflow: Trap 1
	ADD 2,[1]		; no overflow
	JSP 3,.+1		; Trap 1 is 0 in the microcode, 1 in the PRM
	HALT .
```

### ash-trap-last-step

ASH and ASHC: Trap 1 from the last step only.

- Instructions: ASH, ASHC; operands: `lost_bit_before_last_step`.
- Differs: flags:TRAP1, pc.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Trap 1 and Trap 2: each flag word loads them".

Sources:

- DPE9 **[microcode]** (M8620-0-DPE9 rev B, E85, E78; simple.42, ASHL, ASHCL): each step loads Trap 1 with its own overflow, so Trap 1 is the overflow of the last step; Overflow holds.
- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, p. 2-41, ASH, ASHC): Overflow and Trap 1 if any bit of significance is lost.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, ASH): as the PRM.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, kn10ops.c, x_ashflg): as the PRM.
- KS10FPGA **[emulator]** (KS10FPGA 5090e7a1, pcflags.v): Trap 1 as the microcode; Overflow not held.

With traps on, the difference is a trap that the microcode does not take ([measured] 2026-11-28, discrepancies.md). The PRM defines the case, and no DEC diagnostic tests it, so it does not meet the rule for level B (conformance.md). The choice of ks10-core-soft is open.

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[200000,,1]
	ASH 1,2			; the first step overflows, the second does not
	JSP 2,.+1		; with traps on: no trap in the microcode, a trap in the PRM
	HALT .
```

### dmul-trap-old-overflow

DMUL: Trap 1 from an Overflow that was set before.

- Instructions: DMUL; operands: `start_flags` (flags ['AROV']).
- Differs: flags:TRAP1, pc.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Trap 1 and Trap 2: each flag word loads them".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, DMTRAP): after CLR FPD, set Trap 1 if Overflow is set, also from an earlier instruction.
- PRM **[manual]** (PRM 1982, p. 2-78, overflow trapping): the overflow condition sets Trap 1, not the state of the Overflow flag.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, DMUL): Trap 1 only for (-2^70)^2.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, kn10ops.c, op10dmul): as SIMH.

With traps on, the difference is a trap that the microcode takes ([measured] 2026-11-28, discrepancies.md). The PRM defines the case. DSKCF clears the flags with JFCL 17 before each of its two DMUL instructions (DSKCFM, MSUBR; DSKCFT, DMUL - TEST E), so no DEC diagnostic tests it. It does not meet the rule for level B (conformance.md). The choice of ks10-core-soft is open.

Program:

```
	JRST 2,@[400000,,.+1]	; Overflow set, Trap 1 clear
	DMOVE 1,[EXP 0,2]
	DMUL 1,[EXP 0,3]	; no overflow
	JSP 5,.+1		; with traps on: a trap in the microcode, none in the PRM
	HALT .
```

### dmovn-carry

DMOVN: the carry flags of the complement.

- Instructions: DMOVN, DMOVNM; operands: `any`.
- Differs: flags:CRY0,CRY1.
- Level B: Design decision 2026-11-28. The DEC diagnostics do not test the case: DSKCC tests the low words 0 and 400000,,0 (DMVNF, DMVNMF).
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "DMOVN: the carry flags of the complement".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, DBLNGA): the complement with AD FLAGS sets Carry 0 and Carry 1.
- uop **[measured]** (2026-11-27, ks10-core-uop, tests/instructions.rs, flag_cases): Carry 0 and Carry 1.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, DMOVN): no flag.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, inmove.c, i_dmovn): no flag.
- KS10FPGA **[emulator]** (KS10FPGA 5090e7a1, alu.v): no flag.

The uop_soft mask covers every DMOVN and DMOVNM, not only a low word that is not 0.

Program:

```
	DMOVN 1,[EXP 0,5]
	JSP 3,.+1
	HALT .
```

### dmul-carry

DMUL: the carry flags of QMULT.

- Instructions: DMUL; operands: `any`.
- Differs: flags:CRY0,CRY1.
- Level B: The PRM names Overflow and Trap 1 for (-2^70)^2 and no carry flag for DMUL (PRM 1982, p. 2-16). DSKCF checks only Overflow after DMUL: MULTF tests the PC word with TLZE SCR2,AROV (DSKCFT, DMUL - TEST C), and DMUL - TEST E expects Overflow for (-2^70)^2. No DEC diagnostic tests the carry flags (a reading of the KLAD sources, 2026-11-28).
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "DMUL: the carry flags of QMULT".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (simple.42, DMUL, DMUL2, QMULT; M8620-0-DPE9 rev A1, E305): Carry 0 and Carry 1 if a high part is negative.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_cpu.c, DMUL): Overflow and Trap 1 for (-2^70)^2; no carry flag.
- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, kn10ops.c, op10dmul): as SIMH.

Program:

```
	DMOVE 1,[EXP 400000000000,0]
	DMUL 1,[EXP 400000000000,0]	; (-2^70)^2
	JSP 5,.+1
	HALT .
```

### float-unnormalized

Floating point instructions with unnormalized operands.

- Instructions: FAD, FSB, FMP, FDV; operands: `unnormalized_operand`.
- Differs: ac, mem.
- Origin: [`unknowns.md`](unknowns.md), "Floating point instructions with unnormalized operands".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (flt.5): its own handling.
- DSKCB **[manual]** (DSKCB.SEQ page 32, test P7700): FDV of 377400,,777777 by 577400,,777777 gives 777375,,773771.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (docs/unknowns.md): follows the KL10.

The diagnostic vector is level A; the other unnormalized operands are not classified.

Program:

```
	MOVE 1,[377400,,777777]
	FDV 1,[577400,,777777]	; DSKCB P7700: 777375,,773771
	HALT .
```

### pfw-address-high

The page fail word of a memory reference: the address bits above bit 18.

- Instructions: PUSH; operands: `page_fail`.
- Differs: pfw:16-17.
- Origin: [`emulator.md`](emulator.md), "bits 16 and 17 of the page fail word".

Sources:

- microcode **[microcode]** (itspag.98, PFMAP, ADDRESS HIGH/MEMORY): VMA 16 and 17, from the left half of the word that gave the address.
- DPM4 **[manual]** (M8621-0-DPM4 rev B, E183): VMA 14 to 17 load from DP 14 to 17 at each VMA load.
- uop **[measured]** (2026-11-28, ITS boot in step, instruction 11 437 018): 410001,,000637 (ks10-core-soft: 410000,,000637).

The models differ, and the case has no level: whether ITS reads bits 14 to 17 of the page fail word of a memory reference is not checked.

Program:

```
	; With ITS paging on and no access to the page of 10000:
	MOVE 17,[777014,,7777]
	PUSH 17,1		; the page fail word, bits 16-17: 0 or VMA 16-17
	HALT .
```

### tm03-space-tape-mark

TM03: a space that stops at a tape mark.

- Differs: register.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "TM03: a space that stops at a tape mark".

Sources:

- KLH10 **[emulator]** (KLH10 6d733f2, dvtm03.c, tm_cmddon): no error bit.
- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_tu.c, FNC_SPACEF): frame count error (FCE).
- 8080 **[its]** (cmds.m80, MBINT; nmtape.30, MGSPCF): expects FCE after a space.

Program:

```
	; Space Forward of 2 records over a tape mark after the first record;
	; read the TM03 status and error registers.
```

### tm03-read-tape-mark

TM03: a read of a tape mark.

Sources:

- SIMH **[emulator]** (sims 9556eca0, kx10_tu.c, FNC_READ): FCE and the controller transfer error.
- ITS **[its]** (nmtape.30, MGRD1A): the TM03 gives no FC error on READ.

Program:

```
	; Read Forward at a tape mark; read the TM03 status and error
	; registers.
```

### memstat-power-fail-write

Memory status register: the write of POWER FAIL.

- Differs: register.
- Origin: [`discrepancies.md`](discrepancies.md), "Memory status register: the write of POWER FAIL".

Sources:

- KSDEFS **[its]** (ksdefs.194, %KEPWR [R/C]): a write of 1 clears the bit.
- reference card **[manual]** (KS10 reference card, memory status register, bit 12): a write of 1 clears the bit.
- MMC5 **[manual]** (EK-OKS10-TM-002 figure 5-30; M8618-0-MMC5 rev B, E61, E51, E58): a write of 0 clears the bit.
- KS10FPGA **[emulator]** (KS10FPGA 5090e7a1, memstat.sv, statPF): a write of 0 clears the bit.

Program:

```
	SETZ 1,
	IOWR 1,[100000]		; write 0 to the memory status register
	IORD 2,[100000]		; bit 12: POWER FAIL
	HALT .
```
